expected_claims.text: Telehealth use remains above pre-2020 baseline for selected follow-up and behavioral-health services.
Reimbursement conditions improved enough for selected behavioral-health and chronic-care telehealth follow-up services to support selective expansion, though parity is not universal.
The recommendation should shift from pilot-only caution to selective expansion for the targeted follow-up service lines because the reimbursement premise changed.
Licensing, documentation, consent, and workflow constraints still limit broad expansion.
Access and continuity gains do not prove system-wide cost savings, so the recommendation should preserve uncertainty.

Remote monitoring hardware procurement trends justify telehealth expansion.
Employer wellness benefit trends are a core reason to expand clinical telehealth follow-up.

required_tensions.description: The output should preserve the tension between improved access / continuity and uncertain system-wide cost savings.
